full_text: Half of Americans aged 18-29 now live with parents. Welcome to India's normal Living with your parents was once Hollywood's favourite joke. Today, 49 per cent of young Americans are doing exactly that, and India's decades-old family model suddenly looks ahead of its time For decades, Western pop culture treated the idea of a twenty-something living with their parents as the ultimate social faux pas. It was the cinematic trope of the “basement-bound slacker” who couldn’t cut it in the real world. In America, turning 18 meant packing your bags, taking out big loans, and leaving home to prove your mettle. Well, times have officially changed. America is catching up with an age-old Indian reality, and they are doing it fast. According to newdata from the Federal Reservecited byThe Wall Street Journal, over 49 per cent of US adults in the age bracket of 18 to 29 now live with at least one parent. That is up a massive 12 percentage points from 2019. Even more surprising for Western norms, nearly a third of those cozying up in their childhood bedrooms are 25 or older. To anyone from India, this isn’t a crisis or a psychological emergency. It’s just Tuesday. Multigenerational housing has been the backbone of Indian society for years, viewed not as a lack of ambition, but as a source of strength, emotional support, and financial backing. But the carefully choreographed show masked a deep power struggle among hardliners, pragmatists, and opponents of the regime. Each faction is not merely seeking to seize power, but it is also seeking answers to fundamental questions about what the Islamic Republic should be, who should run it, and how it should be governed. As long as Khamenei lived, such questions were largely theoretical. These questions — and the accompanying power struggle — are only thinly veiled and easy to spot. In Shanghai, strong winds and rain swept through the city on Thursday, bringing a slight drop in temperature. Forecasters said the city’s weather is expected to deteriorate from Friday as the outer bands of the typhoon move closer, bringing stronger winds and scattered showers. Although Bavi weakened slightly on Thursday morning, it retained super typhoon status, according to the National Meteorological Centre. The storm is forecast to move northwest at speeds of up to 20km/h (12mph), potentially making landfall in or brushing past Taiwan on Saturday before moving toward Fujian or Zhejiang province.
